paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. Real love for people doesn't stop when you can't be in the room. Paul and his companions were torn away "in person, not in heart," and their longing only got stronger (1 Thessalonians 2:17). They couldn't be there, so they sent Timothy, and they prayed. When you can't show up yourself, you can still send help and still pray.

And look at what Paul wanted most. He wasn't worried about whether the Thessalonians had an easy life. He was worried about whether they'd stand firm, because he had warned them that persecution was coming, and it came (1 Thessalonians 3:3-4). Then Timothy came back with good news about their faith and love, and Paul says, "For now we can go on living, as long as you are standing firm in the Lord" (1 Thessalonians 3:8). Faith that holds through hard seasons is worth more than a season with no trouble. So if your week is rough, baker, that doesn't mean you did something wrong. It means you have a reason to hold on.

Then Paul prays something I want to pray for you: "And may the Lord cause you to increase and overflow with love for one another and for everyone else" (1 Thessalonians 3:12). That love isn't just for the people who are easy to love, and it has a purpose. It's so the Lord can establish your heart "in blamelessness and holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus" (1 Thessalonians 3:13). That's why my ovens stay ready, friend. Keep standing firm, keep loving, and let the Lord do the establishing.
